claim: When an idempotent ingest resolves a primary-key collision by reading the stored row back, a failure of that read must be reported as a retryable internal error, never as a payload conflict, because a conflict verdict tells the client to mint a new id for an event that is already recorded and double-counts spend.
because: LightTrack batch ingest .ok().flatten()-ed the read-back and reported store failures as `conflict: different payload`; fixed in e26d6cb and verified with the api suite (217 tests). The single-event door already propagated the error - the two doors had drifted on exactly the retry semantics the technique exists to protect.

claim: When a write API accepts a boolean control (enabled, locked, frozen), grep for its readers before trusting it: a flag with a setter, a column and a display but no enforcement site is a label, and the fix is to route it through the same cache/path the feature's other per-row policy already uses.
because: LightTrack's Project.enabled was accepted by PUT /v1/projects/:id, persisted by all three stores and shown in listings, and read by nothing on the ingest or auth path; a disabled project's keys kept ingesting. Fixed in aa1b2aa by widening the existing per-project redaction-policy cache into a project-policy cache and checking it on both ingest doors; the grep that found it (`\.enabled` across the API crate) took one call.

claim: When an incremental usage cache folds rows inside a transaction, a rollback must reset the cache (or restore its insertion cursor), because a store that reuses insertion ids after rollback will hand the freed ids to the next events and the advanced cursor makes them invisible - an under-count, not the over-count the naive reading expects.
because: LightTrack SQLite batch admission: `events.id` is TEXT so the implicit rowid is max+1 and a rolled-back batch frees it; the cache's `seen_rowid` stayed past it. A test drove the rollback, proved the rowid reuse, and read $9 from the cache where the full-scan reference read $12. Fixed in ba63d35 by resetting the cache on commit failure. The technique text covers eviction and exactness but says nothing about the fold running inside a transaction that can fail.

claim: when an alert carries a delta a counter has already discarded (a periodic flush of rejected calls), its dedup key must include the flush instant, because a cooldown that suppresses the second flush deletes the only copy of that delta
because: lighttrack: ingest-rejected flushes at 900s under a 3600s cooldown lost 3 of every 4 deltas (store answered Suppressed, no row); fixed by keying on the flush timestamp, pinned by a store-backed test

claim: a multi-tenant HTTP API's credential boundary is its own subject: bearer-key minting (prefix + salted digest, shown once), constant-time compare via fixed-width digests, failed-attempt throttling keyed on a trusted source identity, key capabilities narrower than the tenant, expiry as a distinct code from a wrong guess, a tenant kill switch enforced at the credential, and a scope carried on every store read so a foreign id is not-found rather than forbidden
because: lighttrack: crates/api/src/{auth,guards,auth_scopes,auth_throttle}.rs implement all of these and the registry joined the context to agent-cli-transport / client-state (homonyms); three rounds of findings here (enforced-without-admin-key lockout, per-request last_used write, unpinned error-code contract) had no technique to be judged against

claim: a normalized token-usage record must state whether cached input is a SUBSET of input or ADDITIONAL to it, and every per-provider extractor must convert to that one convention - OpenAI's prompt_tokens includes cached tokens, Anthropic's input_tokens excludes cache_read_input_tokens - or the price book bills the same cache hit two different ways
because: lighttrack: PriceBook::cost_usd_mode computes billable_input = input - cached (subset convention); the Python, Rust and TS Anthropic extractors pass input_tokens through unchanged, so an Anthropic call with input_tokens=1000 and cache_read=800 bills 200 uncached instead of 1000 - the wire type's doc says only 'provider-dependent'
